item.title: High school cellphone ban heads to Georgia governor's desk - Tifton Gazette
item.description: Cellphones will be banned in Georgia public high schools starting in the 2027-28 school year, if Gov. Brian Kemp signs House Bill 1009 into law.

item.title: TCHS teacher named Kiwanis Art Citizen of the Year - Tifton Gazette
item.description: TIFTON — The Kiwanis Club of Tifton has named Tift County High School English teacher Jake Alley as their Kiwanis Art Citizen of the Year. The local chapter of the […]

item.title: Georgia lawmakers pass bill penalizing protests that block roads - Tifton Gazette
item.description: The Georgia House voted Monday to impose tougher punishments on protesters who block streets, approving the bill over objections from legislators who said it infringes on free speech rights.

item.title: Georgians may be able to forgo observing Daylight Saving Time - Tifton Gazette
item.description: Residents of the State Georgia will not have to “spring forward” or “fall back” if HB 154 is put into effect.

item.title: TERRY TURNER: Powers of the President—or not - Tifton Gazette
item.description: The Constitution of the United States took effect on July 21, 1788. It applied to the thirteen former British colonies that had previously suffered through six years of war of rebellion against Britain.

item.title: Servicemembers, spouses to benefit from licensing board settlement - Tifton Gazette
item.description: An agreement between the U.S. Justice Department and 42 Georgia licensing boards will enable spouses to maintain professional licenses when servicemembers relocate to Georgia.

item.title: Blue Devils stumble in doubleheader at Lowndes - Tifton Gazette
item.description: VALDOSTA — The Tift County Blue Devils baseball team struggled to get rolling at the plate in a doubleheader against the Lowndes Vikings Friday afternoon as their losing woes continued.

item.title: Panthers take doubleheader over Brookwood, complete season sweep - Tifton Gazette
item.description: THOMASVILLE — The Tiftarea Panthers baseball team, coming off a strong bounce back performance at home against Brookwood, made the return trip to Thomasville for a doubleheader on Thursday, March 26.

item.title: Two Panthers sign LOIs to play college football - Tifton Gazette
item.description: CHULA — Two seniors of the Tiftarea Panthers football team signed their letters of intent to continue their playing career at the college level on Wednesday, March 25.

item.title: Stallions outpaced by No. 2 Georgia Gwinnett, 10-5 - Tifton Gazette
item.description: LAWRENCEVILLE — The No. 24 ABAC Stallions baseball team went on the road for a midweek top 25 showdown against the No. 2 team in the NAIA, the Georgia Gwinnett College Grizzlies, Tuesday afternoon.

item.title: Blue Devils end losing streak, blast North Bay Haven, 19-1 - Tifton Gazette
item.description: PANAMA CITY, Fla. — The Tift County Blue Devils baseball team took to the beach for a reprieve from region play Tuesday night with a matchup against the North Bay Haven Charter Academy Buccaneers.

item.title: UPDATE: Public school free speech bill honoring Charlie Kirk clears Georgia General Assembly - Tifton Gazette
item.description: A bill that honors conservative activist Charlie Kirk and protects students’ political speech moved closer to becoming law Monday.

item.title: Following the lead of other Southern states, Georgia lawmakers adopt major school literacy initiative - Tifton Gazette
item.description: After watching high school graduation rates soar despite poor reading skills documented in tests, Georgia lawmakers have decided to send tens of millions of dollars to elementary schools to boost literacy rates.

item.title: ABAC homecoming, rodeo set for April 10-11 - Tifton Gazette
item.description: Saddle up, Abraham Baldwin Agricultural College partners. Homecoming, featuring the high-flying Gee Haw Whoa Back Rodeo, makes a return to campus April 10-11 with a full weekend of activities.
